pages.title: Rooms
pages.content:
Four rooms, one wedding

Everything in the building is yours for the day: a ceremony room, the long dining hall, a gravel court and a quiet dressing room.

The North Room

A calm ceremony hall defined by morning light, oak chairs and lime-washed brick.

The North Room seats up to 120 guests along a central aisle facing tall riverside windows. The acoustics are soft and the proportions uncluttered, so spoken vows and a single instrument carry without amplification. It takes twenty minutes to turn around for a different layout.

Ceremonies up to 120 seated

The Long Hall

The main hall: long undyed-linen tables, oak seating, daylight turning to candlelight.

Dinner is served family-style along continuous tables running through the centre of the hall, under fourteen tall arched windows. The timber floor is original, the heating is new, and the double doors open straight onto the Garden Court.

Dinner for up to 96 at long tables

The Garden Court

A gravel courtyard behind old brick walls, with olive trees in planters and warm festoon bulbs.

Drinks after the ceremony, dancing once the tables are moved back, and the next-morning brunch all happen here. It sits beside the wharf edge, so there is a breeze from the river in summer and the bulbs come on at dusk.

Drinks and dancing for up to 140

The Dressing Room

A private suite away from the public rooms, open to the wedding party from 11:00.

Soft daylight, full-length mirrors, generous hanging rails and comfortable seating. It is a place to gather, dress and pause before the day begins, with the door to the Garden Court a few steps away.

For up to 8, from 11:00

Included

Tables, oak chairs, undyed linen and glassware for up to 96 at dinner.

The house team for the whole hire, 11:00 to 00:30: Amara on the day, Rafael at the bar, Tomas for the building. Heating, a step-free route to every room, and a cloakroom by the main doors.

Fees & Dates

pages.title: The Day
pages.content:
A wedding day as it actually runs

Doors open at 11:00 and close at 00:30. In between, the house team moves each room for you.

Morning to midnight

Every wedding here follows the same frame, so you can plan around it and change what you like. Amara keeps the schedule and the running order, and she meets you three times beforehand: six months, eight weeks and ten days before the day.

11:00Doors open to the wedding party. The Dressing Room is yours, and the kitchen starts on lunch for the party.
13:00Guests arrive in the Garden Court. Rafael pours water and something cold; Hana's flowers are already on the tables.
14:00Ceremony in the North Room, usually 30 to 45 minutes.
15:00Drinks in the Garden Court while the Long Hall is finished for dinner.
18:30Dinner in the Long Hall, served family-style along the long tables.
21:00Tables are moved back and the hall becomes the dance floor.
23:30Music ends. Tea, water and the last conversations.
00:30Doors close.

If the weather turns

Every outdoor moment has an indoor twin.

The ceremony can move from the Garden Court to the North Room in twenty minutes, and drinks move to the Long Hall with the double doors left open. Elif and Jonah had 92 guests and an October downpour; nobody was in the wrong room at the wrong time.

Decided by 12:00 on the day

Smaller days, winter days

The same day, quieter.

A Monday to Thursday wedding or a winter day often means fewer guests. Sanne and Theo had 34 around one candlelit table on a January Tuesday. The hire, the hours and the house team are the same; only the fee changes.

Winter day from €5,200

pages.title: Food
pages.content:
One kitchen, cooked in the building

Lucien's kitchen sits behind the Long Hall. Dinner comes straight from it to the table.

Dinner

A three-course seasonal dinner from the house kitchen is €118 per guest. Menus follow the market: Lucien writes them about eight weeks before the day, after tasting with you, and cooks from fresh regional produce.

Dishes arrive on shared plates down the middle of the long tables. Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free and allergy menus are part of the same kitchen, not a separate order.

At the table

Linen, glass, bread and a short menu.

The table is deliberately plain: undyed linen, plain glassware, folded napkins, flowers from Hana. Bread arrives first and wine is poured by Rafael from the bar in the Long Hall.

Three courses, €118 per guest

The next morning

A brunch in the Garden Court for those who stay.

Bread, eggs, fruit, coffee and tea on the long wooden table, at a relaxed hour. It is a good way to see everyone once more before they travel home.

Brunch, €34 per guest

The evening bar

Run by Rafael until the music ends at 23:30.

A short list of wines, beer and non-alcoholic drinks, plus tea and water through the night. Bar service is billed on what is poured; there is no minimum spend.

pages.title: Fees & Dates
pages.content:
What the hall costs

One price per day, with the hire, the linen and the house team included. All prices are in euros, with VAT.

Hire 11:00 to 00:30

Hire includes the whole building, tables, chairs, undyed linen and the house team.

  • SaturdayApril–October€11,500
  • Friday or SundayApril–October€8,900
  • Monday–ThursdayApril–October€6,800
  • Winter dayany day, November–March€5,200

Extras

  • Ceremony onlyNorth Room, 2 hours, Monday–Thursday€2,400
  • Dinnerthree courses, per guest€118
  • Next-morning brunchGarden Court, per guest€34

Terms

A date can be held free for 7 days. To confirm it, we ask for a 30 % deposit. The balance is due 8 weeks before the day.

If you cancel more than 8 weeks before, the deposit is kept and the balance is refunded. Capacity: ceremony up to 120 seated, dinner up to 96, Garden Court up to 140 standing.

pages.title: The People
pages.content:
Seven people look after the building

A small resident team, so the person you meet at the viewing is the person on the day.

The team

  • Ines VargaCo-founder, venue directorEstablished Kasane Venue in spring 2016 after the two-year restoration of Weavers' Hall. She oversees the daily running of the venue and makes sure each couple has the building to themselves.
  • Tomas AchterbergCo-founder, keeper of the buildingDirected the restoration between 2014 and 2016 and looks after the fourteen arched windows, the oak floor and the lime-washed brick.
  • Amara OkonjoWedding coordinatorYour one point of contact from the first viewing to the last song. She holds three planning meetings: six months, eight weeks and ten days before.
  • Priya NairBookings and viewingsWalks couples through the hall in a sixty-minute viewing, Tuesday to Sunday, and manages date holds and the monthly open day.
  • Lucien MarchettiHead of the kitchenLeads the house kitchen: three-course seasonal dinners and next-morning brunches from fresh regional ingredients.
  • Hana KowalczykFlorist in residenceMakes seasonal arrangements and table foliage to suit the daylight, and the dried-petal confetti used in the Garden Court.
  • Rafael DuarteEvening host and barRuns drinks, the dinner service and the bar until the music ends at 23:30, and keeps the evening unhurried.

One wedding a day

Why the team is small.

We host one wedding a day on purpose. Everyone on the team is in the building from 11:00 to the last guest, and everyone knows your names, your order of the day and which cousin needs the step-free route.

pages.title: The Building
pages.content:
A wool exchange, built in 1908

Weavers' Hall on Calder Wharf, restored between 2014 and 2016 to hold one wedding a day.

History

Weavers' Hall was built in 1908 on Calder Wharf as a regional wool exchange. Merchants and shearers traded fleece under northern daylight that came through fourteen tall arched windows.

In 1971 it became a textile store, and from 2003 to 2013 it stood empty beside the water. Between 2014 and 2016 Ines Varga and Tomas Achterberg restored it: they removed later partitions, uncovered the oak floor and the brickwork, lime-washed the walls, and added heating, private dressing rooms and a kitchen.

Kasane Venue opened in spring 2016. The name means layers: rooms, light and days laid one over another.

The hall

Fourteen windows, an oak floor and lime-washed walls.

The floor is the original oak, the walls are lime-washed brick, and the daylight does most of the work. Heating and the kitchen are new, and kept out of sight.

Built 1908 · restored 2014–2016

The Garden Court

The doors open straight out.

Gravel, olive trees and old brick, with the river a few steps beyond the gate. The court is part of every wedding hire.

pages.title: Viewings
pages.content:
Come and walk through the hall

A viewing takes sixty minutes with Priya, Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 17:00, by appointment.

Open day

On the first Saturday of every month, 11:00 to 15:00, the doors are open and you can walk in without an appointment. Priya, Amara and Lucien are in the building to answer questions.

Request a viewing

Write to Priya with two or three possible days.

Send us your names, your rough date, the number of guests and two or three days that suit you for a viewing. Priya replies within two working days. We do not publish a phone number; the office answers email Tuesday to Friday, 9:30 to 17:30.

hello@kasanevenue.example

Email Priya

From viewing to wedding

After the viewing you can hold your date free for 7 days. To confirm it, you pay a 30 % deposit. Amara then meets you three times: six months, eight weeks and ten days before the day.

pages.title: Visit & Contact
pages.content:
Weavers' Hall, Calder Wharf

22 Calder Wharf, Halbrook. The big wooden double doors face the river.

Hours

  • Viewingsby appointmentTue–Sun 10:00–17:00
  • Open dayfirst Saturday of every month11:00–15:00
  • Officeby emailTue–Fri 9:30–17:30
  • Wedding hireone wedding a day11:00–00:30

Getting here

Calder Wharf is a flat ten-minute walk from the centre of Halbrook along the river. There is no parking on the wharf; cars and taxis can set down guests at the gate. The Garden Court gate gives a step-free route into every room.

Write to hello@kasanevenue.example. We do not publish a phone number, so everything is in writing and nothing is lost.

pages.title: Questions
pages.content:
Questions couples ask

Short answers, with numbers. For anything else, write to us.

Before you book

How many guests can you host?

Ceremonies up to 120 seated in the North Room, dinner up to 96 in the Long Hall, and drinks or dancing for up to 140 in the Garden Court.

Do you host more than one wedding a day?

No. The building is yours alone from 11:00 to 00:30.

How long can we hold a date?

Seven days, free. A 30 % deposit confirms it.

What does the hire include?

The whole building, tables, chairs, undyed linen and the house team. Dinner and brunch are priced per guest.

When does the music end?

At 23:30. Doors close at 00:30.

What if we cancel?

More than 8 weeks before the day, the deposit is kept and the balance is refunded.

Can we bring our own caterer?

The house kitchen cooks every wedding dinner, so that the timing of the day stays in one pair of hands.

Is the building step-free?

Yes. The Garden Court gate gives a step-free route into every room.

posts.title: Elif & Jonah
posts.excerpt: An October Saturday with 92 guests, where autumn rain moved the ceremony indoors.
posts.content:
Elif and Jonah chose an October Saturday for 92 guests. The forecast said rain, and by midday it had settled in over Calder Wharf, so the ceremony moved from the Garden Court into the North Room, which takes twenty minutes to turn around.

Guests arrived at 13:00 under umbrellas and were handed linen napkins to dry their hands. The vows were spoken at 14:00 facing the tall window, and drinks followed in the Long Hall with the double doors open to the wet gravel. Dinner for all 92 was served at 18:30 along the long undyed-linen tables.

posts.title: Sanne & Theo
posts.excerpt: A quiet winter Tuesday for 34 guests, gathered around one candlelit table.
posts.content:
Sanne and Theo married on a January Tuesday with 34 guests. On winter days the hall is hired from 11:00 to 00:30 like any other, but with fewer people the dinner was laid as one short table beneath the tall windows.

By 16:30 the windows had turned blue and the candles were lit. Lucien sent out three courses of winter vegetables and slow-cooked lamb, and the music ended early, well before the 23:30 limit.

posts.title: Marisol & Ade
posts.excerpt: A June garden ceremony for 120 guests with dried petals under bright summer skies.
posts.content:
Marisol and Ade married in the Garden Court in June with 120 guests, the most the courtyard holds standing. Hana dressed the olive trees in dried petals, which are the only confetti allowed on the gravel.

After the ceremony the party moved through the open double doors into the Long Hall for dinner, and came back outside at 21:00 when the tables were moved back and the dancing began.
